newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise in active trade, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise in active trade, seen drifting.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the second session running on speculative buying spurred by Friday's Dow jump with analysts expecting possible further gains to provoke profit-taking and keep the market in its sideways drift.
The main market's WIG index rose 1.2 percent, to 16,744.3, and turnover was stable at 188.6 million zlotys ($60.8 million) on all three markets as 73 issues rose, 15 fell and six were flat.
Analysts said a strong uptrend before general elections scheduled for September was unlikely but Polish stocks were attractive enough to avoid significant falls.

"I believe we are in a horizontal trend and I think it might last until the polls," said Roman Sosnowski of Bank Staropolski brokerage. He saw the market locked between 100 -session and 45-session moving averages of 16,000 and 17,000.

Analysts said some garment makers extended their recent rise with Prochnik jumping 10 percent on Monday as the long-neglected stocks began to look undervalued despite uninspiring fundamentals and started attracting some interest.
Vistula, which traded at 6.7 times historic earnings, rose 4.6 percent on Monday while Wolczanka, trading at eight times historic earnings against 15.7 of the whole market, jumped seven percent.
But analysts said growth of the smaller and less liquid stocks such as garment makers was unlikely to cause significant growth of the whole index in the longer-term.

They said banks, which accounted for about 40 percent of the main index weighing, were likely to suffer from recent central bank decision to increase mandatory reserves on zloty term deposits and all foreign currency deposits from April 30.
Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy did not trade on Monday after last week Allied Irish Banks (AIB) announced a public tender offer for its shares.
